//ApiBaseUrl: appsettings.json points at the deployed API, and ApiFallbackHandler.cs treats a 500 from it as transient. So a local run that means to talk to its own API instead walks the network to a host it is not running. Point the session-cookie proxy at the Development API profile (http://localhost:5184) and a stopped local API fails as itself.
//BackupApiBaseUrl: Blank on purpose. ApiFallbackHandler retries on any non-empty backup, and its backup is the live Azure API - so with a value here, a local sign-in whose API is down silently submits real credentials to production infrastructure and shows the page a confusing error from a database you did not create. The primary+backup failover is a deployed-web-tier behaviour, not a local-development one.
